h: Conquering the Barriers of Mind and Heart

p: אֵלֶּה הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹ׳
"These are the words that Moshe spoke," etc.
king of the Emori, who dwells in Cheshbon,
and Og, king of the Bashan,
אֲשֶׁר יוֹשֵׁב בְּעַשְׁתָּרוֹת בְּאֶדְרֶעִי (דְּבָרִים א, א–ד)
who dwells in Ashtaros, in Edre'i" (Devarim 1:1–4).
We need to understand why it says
Also, do we not already know this
that he had already conquered Sichon?
Also the expression "who dwells," in the present tense
but he had already smitten him,
so the expression "dwells" does not fit.
נֶאֱמַר גַּם כֵּן אֲשֶׁר יוֹשֵׁב וְגוֹ׳
is the beginning of Mishneh Torah,
which Moshe said on his own
and it is the seventh book,
as is known that the section "Vayehi binso'a"
הוּא סֵפֶר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ (שַׁבָּת קטז, א)
is a book in its own right (Shabbos 116a);
and it corresponds to the middah of Malchus:
פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ
"the mouth — we call it Torah she'b'al peh"
And in it are words of rebuke,
"For in much wisdom is much anger";
one must of necessity stand against it
the wisdom that is in the mind
with the understanding that is in the heart,
so that it enters the depths of the heart.
We have already spoken of this above,
which are the mind and the heart.
the revelation of Torah she'b'al peh
after the subduing of the kelipos
of the mind and the heart,
Now after the war against Sichon
וְדָרְשׁוּ עַל זֶה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא עח, ב)
And they expounded on this (Bava Basra 78b):
these are those who rule over their yetzer;
the loss of a mitzvah against its reward,
and the gain of a sin against its loss.
you will be built in this world
and established for the World to Come.
אִם מֵשִׂים אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כְּעַיִר זֶה
if a person makes himself like this young donkey
the wicked one said, there is no One on high;
'is lost' — the reckoning of the world," etc.
that he says there is no reckoning
"there is no judgment and no Judge."
And this is the kelipah of Sichon,
which is the place of thought in the mind,
and he does not let a person
that there is yet a World to Come.
And now, after he smote Sichon
"Come, let us calculate the reckoning of the world."
from our master, teacher and Rebbe, the holy one
of Izhbitza, of blessed and holy memory,
that there is yet another world,
who is saved in all his affairs.
שֶׁעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ חֲזַ״ל (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ, א)
a share in the World to Come;
and these are the ones who have no share:
one who says there is no resurrection of the dead
and that the Torah is not from Heaven,
One may say that these three
which oppose the three upper ones,
are not among the community of Yisrael
rather, they are of the Erev Rav,
as is stated in the Midrash
it is certain that he is not
And all this is also alluded to
in the pasuk "Come to Cheshbon" mentioned above.
is one who follows smooth talk,
that finds favor in his eyes;
but in truth from this branches out
שֹׁרֶשׁ פּוֹרֶה רֹאשׁ וְלַעֲנָה (דְּבָרִים כט, יז)
"a root that bears gall and wormwood" (Devarim 29:17),
כִּי נֹפֶת תִּטּוֹפְנָה שִׂפְתֵי זָרָה וְגוֹ׳
"For the lips of a strange woman drip honey," etc.;
and this is the aspect of apikores.
And from this he comes afterward
to deny the resurrection of the dead,
which is the aspect of "the reckoning is lost":
that there is no judgment and no Judge,
since "the way of the wicked prospers" (Yirmiyahu 12:1).
And this corresponds to the aspect of Chochmah of holiness;
for in truth great wisdom is needed for this,
to calculate "the loss of a mitzvah"
in all the affairs of this world,
only that it should be worthwhile for him
for the sake of the reward of the World to Come;
meaning that even though the way of the wicked prospers,
because of the loss of the World to Come.
And corresponding to the aspect of Binah in the heart
הוּא הָאוֹמֵר אֵין תּוֹרָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
is one who says the Torah is not from Heaven.
וְעוֹד דָּרְשׁוּ עַל פָּסוּק הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל (בְּמִדְבַּר כא, כח)
And they further expounded on the pasuk mentioned above (Bamidbar 21:28):
'the lords of the high places of Arnon'
For the kelipah of Moav is in desire,
and from this one comes to haughtiness,
and your heart grow haughty and you forget."
"We have heard of the pride of Moav,
it is alluded to in the pasuk:
"the lords of the high places of Arnon"
"For Arnon is the border of Moav";
and from this one comes to "And we shot at them,"
that there is no One on high,
the reckoning of the world is lost,
"and your heart grow haughty and you forget,"

p: Let us return to the matter mentioned above,
opposes the aspect of Chochmah of holiness,
that is, it opposes the thought in the mind.
And this is "after he had smitten Sichon,
it does not say that he killed him,
only in the language of smiting,
meaning that he sapped his strength;
there is not yet the ultimate refinement
until the time of the End,
And for this reason it says
even after he had smitten him,
for the root of the kelipah
And likewise "Og, king of the Bashan,
who dwells in Ashtaros, in Edre'i"
meaning that he is the opponent
of the aspect of Binah in the heart,
that is, to make the heart like stone,
so that it is not moved by words of Torah.
וְעַל זֶה רוֹמֵז רַשִׁ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה (דְּבָרִים א, ד)
And to this Rashi, of blessed memory, alludes (Devarim 1:4):
"Ashtaros is an expression of crags and hardness,
Now we have already spoken of this,
that the aspects of king and kohen in holiness
correspond to the heart and the mind;
corresponds to the mind of Chochmah,
which is why, when Aharon died,
the king of Arad came to fight,
And the king corresponds to the heart,
as is stated in Sefer Yetzirah:
is like a king in the land."
And this is the kelipah of Og,
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and he is the aspect of the heart
words of Torah are absorbed into the heart.
